component_notes.ED26-SRC-050-0004-C012: Source sec. 12 (author's version pp. 22-24). Written: body handbook/parts/p03/random-structures-and-limit-laws-w03-p03-071.tex L1-495 (def -assumptions, -gord, thm -no-zero-one, def -arithmetizable, thm -unique, def -literal, thm -literal-fails, def -clean, thm -witness, -representation, def -block-encoding L230, thm -kary L252 with remark L259-273, thm -upper, -log-mod, lemma -prime L324, cor -prime-graph L352, def -sentence, thm -chs, example -u-three, warning -speed, def -common-nbhd, lemma -all-sizes, proofboundary -sparse-outline); annex L1-512 (new: annex -kary L252, -prime L312, -prime-graph L362). Block 2 added: the k-ary remark of p. 23 with exact hypotheses (block encoding, u <= U_k(n)) and complete proof; explicit statement that representability of every ternary relation up to a constant multiple of (log n)^{1/3} is not established; the p. 23 examples (u prime, u a Fermat prime) as formulas with proofs and their almost sure transfer to G_<(n,1/2) for u <= 0.9L. Missing (unchanged): a complete proof of the source's outlined nonconvergence for G(n,n^{-1/4}) through N(x1,x2,x3,x4) (p. 24): that each R_u acts like an independent random ternary relation of density 1-e^{-1}; that <,+,* are almost surely represented on S of size up to ln^{1/3} n (including the source's own open point of representing the asymmetric < and the non-symmetric + by relations symmetric in their arguments); that a maximal arithmetizable N(x1,...,x4) has size Theta(ln^{1/3} n); the first-order BIGGER comparison at p=n^{-1/4}; and the resulting nonconvergent sentence.
